# v1.0.0 — QR *and* barcodes, a stable API, and a decoder that survives hostile input

The API stops changing here. What that promise covers is written down in the
[compatibility policy](https://github.com/wirunrom/barqr/blob/v1.0.0/README.md#compatibility).

**The package moved to `__NEW_PKG__`.** `@wirunrom/hqr-generate` is deprecated;
its last release is 0.6.0. See
[MIGRATION.md](https://github.com/wirunrom/barqr/blob/v1.0.0/MIGRATION.md) —
the import path and the function names changed, nothing else did.

| | 0.6.0 | 1.0.0 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Package | `@wirunrom/hqr-generate` | **`__NEW_PKG__`** |
| Symbologies | QR | **QR + nine 1D formats** |
| Reading | QR only | **QR, 1D, DataMatrix, Aztec, PDF417** |
| Frameworks | React | React **and Vue / Nuxt** |
| Decoding a 1.2 MB crafted PNG | 976 MB, 2.2 s | **refused in <1 ms** |
| Reachable panic in the decoder | yes | **fixed** |
| Tests | 37 · 45 · 15 (manual) | 4 suites · 52 · **19 headless in CI** |
| CI | 2 platforms | **3 platforms + MSRV + weekly fuzzing** |

## 📊 Barcodes

Nine 1D symbologies — Code 128, Code 39 (with or without check character),
Code 93, Code 11, Codabar, EAN-8, EAN-13 and ITF — as PNG, SVG or the raw bar
pattern.

```js
await barcodePng("SKU-0001", { format: "code128" });
await barcodeSvg("012345678901", { format: "ean13" }); // check digit computed and printed
```

The encoder grows from 85 KB to 100 KB gzipped for all nine, because a 1D
symbology is lookup tables and bit patterns next to the Reed-Solomon and masking
machinery QR needs. It reuses the same renderers: whole pixels per module, runs
merged before the encoder sees them.

Each format **rejects** data it cannot represent rather than mangling it —
Code 39 has no lowercase, EAN-13 needs 12 or 13 digits — with
`INVALID_BARCODE_DATA` naming the symbology that refused. EAN computes its check
digit from 12 digits and prints it, so the digits under the bars always agree
with the bars. PNG carries no human-readable text: drawing it needs a font, and
a font is larger than everything else in the binary put together.

**Reading them** is `decodeAny` / `decodeAnyAll`, and the camera scanner takes
`formats: "any"`. That decoder is a *third* WASM module, not a replacement:
reading QR alone stays at 267 KB gzipped, reading everything costs 598 KB, and
nothing fetches it until you ask.

## 🔒 Security

Two real vulnerabilities, both found preparing this release, both reachable from
`decode` with input a user could supply.

**Unbounded allocation from a small file.** A compressed image describes a
canvas rather than containing one. A 1.2 MB PNG declaring 16000×16000 made the
decoder allocate **976 MB** and burn 2.2 s of CPU before concluding there was no
QR code — roughly an 800× amplification. `image`'s own `max_alloc` did not help,
because the largest allocation was this crate's `to_rgba8()` call, downstream of
that accounting. Dimensions are now checked against the header before any pixels
are read; over 40 megapixels is refused with `IMAGE_TOO_LARGE`, allocating
nothing.

**A reachable panic.** Fuzzing produced RGBA input that panicked inside
`rqrr` 0.7: `Perspective::map` asserts its result fits in an `i32`, but that
value is computed from image data. This matters more than an ordinary dependency
bug, because `wasm32-unknown-unknown` has `panic-strategy: abort` — a panic in
the decode path takes the whole WASM instance with it and **cannot be caught**.
One crafted image would end decoding for the life of a page, or of a server
request. Fixed by moving to `rqrr` 0.10; the input is kept as a regression test.

Fuzzing is permanent now: two `cargo-fuzz` targets, a seed corpus generated from
real encoder output, and a weekly CI run.

## ✨ Vue and Nuxt

`__NEW_PKG__/vue` mirrors the React layer hook for hook.

```vue
<script setup>
import { useQr, useBarcode } from "__NEW_PKG__/vue";
const { src } = useQr(() => props.url, { size: 320 });
</script>
```

The SSR guard is the substance. `watchEffect` runs during server rendering while
React's `useEffect` does not, so an unguarded composable would try to `fetch()`
the WASM binary mid-render and take down every Nuxt page using it. Generation is
deferred to the client; for QR in the server-rendered HTML, call the synchronous
Node API from a server route.

Verified against Nuxt 4.5 with **no bundler configuration** — no
`nitro.externals`, no `build.transpile`.

## 💥 Breaking

- **The package name.** See MIGRATION.md.
- **Every function is renamed** to say which symbol family it belongs to:
  `generatePng` → `qrPng`, `generateSvg` → `qrSvg`, `generateModules` →
  `qrModules`, `generateMany` → `qrMany`. Hooks follow: `useGenerate` → `useQr`,
  `useQrScanner` → `useScanner`. The bare `generate` alias and the 0.5
  snake_case names are gone. **Every option keeps its name.**
- **Images over 40 megapixels are refused** with `IMAGE_TOO_LARGE`.
- **Scanner results are normalised** onto `{ text, format, points }` across both
  decoders; the QR path's `corners` is now `points`.
- **Rust MSRV is 1.88**, corrected from a declared 1.85 that was never true —
  `image` has required 1.88 for some time, so `--features decode` could not have
  built there. The new CI job caught it on its first run.
- **Rust:** error enums are `#[non_exhaustive]`; `render_svg(&QrBitmap)` is
  removed — it emitted one `<rect>` per module, 143 KB against 5.2 KB.

## 🧪 Testing

- **4 Rust suites** — sizing, 1-bit scanline clearing against a naive reference,
  logo budgets, QR round trips across every ECC level and size, and barcode
  round trips through the any-format decoder for every symbology.
- **52 package tests** — the shipped entry points, `exports` resolution, the
  ESM/CJS boundary, every payload builder including PromptPay's TLV structure
  and CRC, and Vue SSR through `vue/server-renderer`.
- **19 browser tests, headless in CI** — WASM over HTTP, canvas round trips,
  object-URL lifetimes, the scanner reading both a QR code and a barcode from a
  canvas-backed `MediaStream`, and every composable in a mounted Vue app.
- **Two framework fixtures** that install the packed tarball and import by
  package name: `tests/my-app` (Next.js) and `tests/nuxt-app` (Nuxt). Between
  them they have caught three bugs no unit test could see.
- CI on Linux, macOS and Windows, at the declared MSRV, with a bundle size
  budget that fails the build.

## Still verified by hand, not by CI

**PromptPay** payloads are checked for TLV structure and against the standard
CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE vector, and they round-trip through the decoder — but no
automated test can put one in front of a real banking app. Confirm before taking
payments. The same goes for the **camera scanner** on physical hardware: it is
tested against a canvas-backed `MediaStream`, which exercises every line of the
pump, but not a real sensor.
